metadata.summary: If there is one position that highlights the growth of the women's game in England, it is the competition for the half-back spot at the Rugby League World Cup.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: England Women's half-back dilemma as Jenna Foubister, Izzy Rowe and Georgia Roche head into competition in form | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Rugby League World Cup: England Women's half-back dilemma as Jenna Foubister, Izzy Rowe and Georgia Roche head into competition in form England Women have three outstanding half-back options for the upcoming Rugby League World Cup, with Jenna Foubister, Izzy Rowe and Georgia Roche all vying for a place in the side; their campaign gets under way against Wales on October 17 with Izzy Rowe and Georgia Roche starting Megan Wellens Sports Journalist @MegWellensX Wednesday 14 October 2026 13:45, UK Image: Georgia Roche, Jenna Foubister and Izzy Rowe - credit SWpix If there is one position that highlights the growth of the women's game in England, it is the competition for the half-back spot at the Rugby League World Cup. Two Wigan stars provide one option, with Woman of Steel Jenna Foubister joined by her best friend and Warriors half-back partner Izzy Rowe. Then there's NRLW star and former Woman of Steel Georgia Roche, who has been tearing it up on the other side of the world. It is a selection headache that England Women head coach Stuart Barrow welcomes as he prepares his side for three pool games, with a place in the semi-finals at stake. messages.text: What is wrong with Bruno Fernandes?

metadata.summary: A day before Manchester United's trip to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, the club issued a statement on captain Bruno Fernandes. It spoke of an "injury niggle" but stressed there was "nothing to worry about". His performance on the night suggested otherwise.
metadata.content: Bruno Fernandes: What has happened to the form of Man Utd's best player - and should Michael Carrick drop him? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Bruno Fernandes: What has happened to the form of Man Utd's best player - and should Michael Carrick drop him? Bruno Fernandes has suffered a worrying dip in form as Manchester United have struggled for momentum this season - time for Michael Carrick to drop his captain? Watch Leeds vs Man Utd live on Sky Sports on Super Sunday from 1pm; kick-off 2pm Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Wednesday 14 October 2026 15:36, UK Image: What has happened to Bruno Fernandes? A day before Manchester United's trip to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, the club issued a statement on captain Bruno Fernandes. It spoke of an "injury niggle" but stressed there was "nothing to worry about". His performance on the night suggested otherwise. Perhaps the reference to an injury was meant to mediate the criticism that has begun to engulf last year's Premier League player of the season. His form has become an unexpected problem for Michael Carrick, a manifestation of where Man Utd stand more broadly. So often United's saviour, Fernandes is currently his side's scourge, the issue being that if he is not contributing offensively, he offers virtually nothing else.
